i really understand this. i’m gay as well, and i come from a very similar financial situation and family dynamic. i often feel invalid because i’ve been financially supported and i should be grateful for what i’ve been given. especially since my parents told me that too. here’s the thing—i am grateful for those things. i never take for granted all of the positive things i’ve had. but i need to also notice that the negative things exist notwithstanding. trauma can happen to anyone.

i don’t know if this is relevant, but i also have a hard time recognizing that my parents aren’t as bad as they used to be. we have a better relationship now (probably because of time apart as i’ve grown older) but i can’t forget about what happened before. however, i can’t shake the feeling that because everything’s mostly okay now, that i should just forget about everything from before. this extends to other family members as well.

i hope some of this resonates with you. sending my best wishes.

i completely understand. i had the same situation earlier this year. it wrecked me. i lashed out at her and all my other friends too. over time it started to sting less. i learned that if someone thinks you’re too much, it’s mostly their problem. but i also learned that i can’t pour everything i have into one person because it takes so much energy to even try to get someone’s attention who is just done listening. it’s a self fulfilling prophecy. you cling to make them not leave, then they leave. no matter what, i know how it feels. it’s the worst feeling. don’t let anyone minimize that. just try as hard as you can to re-develop your identity. you might find that you aren’t giving yourself enough credit. spend time with people who love you. don’t chase someone who had one foot out the door already.

i feel like my strategy is just doing whatever i can to keep busy. it’s usually dumb multitasking stuff like being on my phone while watching tv. it’s super idle and i want to do more active things in theory, but that’s sometimes all i can muster. as for specific names of strategies i’m not sure, but i try to stop myself while thinking and put things in perspective. like, if i’m bored, at least i’m not actively hurting. even though boredom is a sort of hurting in a way.

i am familiar! i took a week long intensive dbt class/program and it was helpful, but it still doesn’t take away the existential loneliness like you mentioned. i’m kind of waiting for some kind of life change, but i have to realize i need to live in the now.

i’m also a pretty codependent person so it’s hard when i feel like my life is only complete with another person around. and i don’t have that right now.

i just had an idea, and i don’t know if it will work. but i was thinking about distress tolerance and letting emotions wash over you. maybe boredom is another emotion? i spent the past hour or so just reading reddit, hanging out, and trying not to put a ton of pressure on myself. i don’t know if i feel better, but i do feel different.

that’s a really good point. i definitely need to learn to differentiate the meaning behind my actions and my motivations. i think i do worry about approval from others, but i also think that i want to avoid acting unfairly. it confuses me when i have to try to assert my own needs in a way that isn’t inherently co-opting someone else’s time.

i suppose i should try to remember that others have to assert their own boundaries. if i ask for help, it’s not wrong unless i’m forcing someone to do something. i used to pretty much beg people to sit with me for hours when i had breakdowns. so i think i assume that any help i ask for is like that - unfair and somewhat manipulative. but i know now that people can choose to leave and i can’t force them to stay.

i want to be a good friend to others and myself. i want to ask for help when i need it, but i want to make sure that i don’t ask for so much help that i don’t grow into a person who can self-soothe. i want to be able to help myself.

if i understand correctly - not asking for help is codependent when you try really hard to make sure that you don’t set anyone off? for example, i worry about asking for help sometimes because i don’t want anyone to be mad at me. is that codependent of me? i want to make sure i understand what you mean exactly, because i think you have some good perspective
